calls.reason: OpenAI's March 2023 plugins post confirms a model-accessible Python interpreter, but no record verifies that Hinton's 'huge mistake' remark covered this kind of tool integration, and that is half the claim.
The claim is hedged ('from what I can tell'), and the packet offers only the DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3 reports as examples, with no count showing most models rely heavily on symbolically generated data.
xAI's launch chart gives no defined compute units or controlled series, and xAI describes smooth gains, so diminishing returns from pure scaling can't be judged from this evidence.
A January 2025 survey and a June 2025 paper both treat symbol grounding as an open foundational problem without shared criteria for a solution; Steels's partial-solution view is heavily qualified.
The peer-reviewed PAL study shows the solve rate falls from 72.0 to 23.2 when the model simulates the Python runtime, so executing code symbolically clearly helped on some tasks.
The forecast has no deadline or threshold, and the only evidence is a usage study ending July 2025, which doesn't isolate substantial changes after the post.
